memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Noah built an altar to the Lord and, taking some of all the clean animals and clean birds, he sacrificed burnt offerings on it. - Gen 8:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The very first thing Noah does on the renewed earth is worship. Before planting a field, before building a house, before anything else, he builds an altar and offers sacrifices to the Lord. His first response to deliverance is gratitude poured out in worship. This tells us everything about Noah's heart - he knew who had saved him, and he gave God the first and the best.

Notice the cost of this worship. Noah offered "some of all the clean animals" - precious creatures he had carefully kept alive through the flood, given back to God in thanksgiving. True worship often costs us something. Noah did not offer God his leftovers but his best, out of a heart overflowing with gratitude for God's mercy.

What is our first response when God brings us through a hard season? Too often we rush on to the next thing, forgetting to stop and thank the God who carried us. Noah shows us a better way - to make worship our first priority, to build an altar of thanksgiving before we build anything else.

This altar also points forward. Noah's burnt offering foreshadows the once-for-all sacrifice of Jesus, who offered Himself to God on our behalf (Eph 5:2). Because of His finished work, we now come to God not with slaughtered animals but with "a sacrifice of praise" (Heb 13:15). After every storm God brings us through, let our first act be worship.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What is usually your first response after God brings you through a trial?
- How can you make grateful worship your first priority this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when You carry me through the storms of life, let my first response be worship. Thank You for the finished sacrifice of Jesus. Receive my sacrifice of praise and my grateful heart.
